exposure: Nulliparous women with singleton, cephalic, term fetuses (Robson category 2)
Nulliparous women with singleton, cephalic, term fetuses with induction of labor (Robson category 2a)
Women with a prior uterine scar (Robson category 5)
Type of care (centers with interprofessional care including midwives vs centers without midwives)
cohort: 96,792 births from the National Institute of Child and Human Development Consortium on Safe Labor data from 2002 to 2008.
finding: Women receiving care in centers with interprofessional teams including midwives had lower rates of labor induction, lower overall cesarean birth rates, and higher rates of vaginal birth after cesarean compared to women receiving care in centers without midwives.
